The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

French Senate blocks new crypto tax and wallet list critics called a kidnapping risk. The government opposed the measures citing existing EU data-sharing rules and non-legal tender status, leaving the 2027 budget open. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

'This time actually seems different': Crypto veterans brace for more pain as bitcoin tumbles. Crypto sentiment is near rock bottom, but Galaxy sees room for a deeper slide and even longtime crypto bulls are wary of buying amid fears of AI and quantum computing. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

EU bank watchdog seeks European Commission rules for crypto firms offering DeFi lending. The EBA renewed its call for the commission to propose rules for crypto firms granting client access to DeFi, particularly lending protocols. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ukrainian lawmakers pass crypto tax and regulation bill expected to bring in $330 million. Lawmaker Yaroslav Zhelezniak said he expects roughly $330 million (15 billion hryvnias) in added budget revenue, though the time frame remains unclear. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto Long & Short: Bitcoin investors can’t keep ignoring Japan. Yen-funded carry trades ran an estimated $250 billion before the August 2024 selloff, and the Bank of Japan's policy rate is now around 1.25%. Phillip Lord of Bitcoin Japan explains how yen funding conditions reach bitcoin, and the shareholder test Japanese companies' bitcoin treasury strategies should have to pass. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb warns of phishing after deeper October breach probe. South Korea's second-largest crypto exchange said its trading systems were not breached, but stolen customer records could already be being used in future scams. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $60,149 with a +0.27% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,684.94 with a -0.00% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.title: Crypto Markets React to Fed Rate Hike Expectations and Inflation Forecasts
items.description: Nexo U.S. head Neil Steinhardt said on Tuesday that the dollar, interest-rate expectations and fund flows remained unchanged. Steinhardt said Wednesday's core PCE reading would affect the dollar and rate expectations. Steinhardt identified $62,000 to $64,000 as the bitcoin price area buyers needed to regain. Steinhardt identified the weekend low near $55,000 as the downside reference level. [...] Crypto markets react to Fed rate hike expectations and new inflation data, with a 0.25% hike priced in for December. The October core PCE report, due Nov. 28, is expected to show a rise to 3.2% annually, up from 3.1% in September. A 60% chance of a January hike remains. Bitcoin has dropped 24% this month, trading below $60,000. Analysts say a PCE reading in line with forecasts may not move markets much, but a miss could deepen losses. XRP has formed a death cross, raising bear market fears. The [...] Forecasts tracked by The Wall Street Journal put October's annual core inflation rate at 3.2%, compared with 3.1% in September. Forecasts put annual headline inflation at 3.8% for October, compared with September's 3.6%. The anticipated December rate increase would bring the Fed's benchmark borrowing rate to between 4% and 4.25%. Market pricing assigns roughly a 60% probability to another increase in January. JPMorgan expects an additional increase in March.
